project_evidence.project_name_en: Danish Fields and Cottonwood solar power plants
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Commissioned solar power plants with co-located battery storage in southeast Texas
project_evidence.snippet_en: In 2024, TotalEnergies commissioned Danish Fields (720 MW) and Cottonwood (455 MW), two solar power plants with co-located battery storage in southeast Texas. These new projects are part of a portfolio of more than 8 GW of renewable assets in operation in the country.

project_evidence.project_name_en: Korea DS Division solar PPA
project_evidence.measure_name_en: PPA with SK E&S and Samsung C&T for renewable energy from a 60 MW solar power plant
project_evidence.snippet_en: The DS Division signed a PPA with SK E&S in Nov. 2023 and with Samsung C&T in Mar. 2024 to supply approximately 76.2 GWh of renewable energy annually from a 60 MW solar power plant for 20 years for a total of 1,466 GWh of renewable energy, starting in 2025. So far, Samsung has installed a total of 2.8 MW of solar power generation facilities and generated 2.8 GWh of energy in 2023 for on-site use.

project_evidence.snippet_en: Cigna reports that it is sourcing renewables and purchasing Energy Attribute Certificates (EACs), committed to sourcing 100% renewable electricity by 2030, joined the global RE100 pledge in 2022, and by the end of 2024 sourced approximately 52% of its global power needs from renewable electricity. The report also states it continues to explore long-term renewable energy procurement agreements, including power purchase agreements and onsite renewables where plausible.

The report states that carbon intensity reduction in its proprietary real-estate equity and debt portfolio resulted from increased renewable energy utilization and energy-efficiency improvements. project_evidence.project_name_en: Design and materials roadmap
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Using recycled lithium, zinc, rare earth elements, and low-carbon materials in products
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report attributes 6.2M avoided emissions to low-carbon materials in the Apple comprehensive carbon footprint graphic.
project_evidence.snippet_en: We design our products to be less carbon intensive by prioritizing the use of recycled and renewable content and low-carbon materials. Our progress: More than doubled the use of certified recycled lithium and zinc shipped in our products in 2024. iPhone 16 uses more than 95 percent recycled lithium in the battery, a first for Apple.

project_evidence.subtype_en: Process gas treatment and process upgrade
project_evidence.project_name_en: DS Division process gas treatment expansion
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Expanded RCS process gas treatment facilities and high-efficiency RCS catalyst development
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report places process gas treatment expansion in the DS Division GHG Emission Reduction Roadmap and states the roadmap aims to achieve net zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions for the DS Division.
project_evidence.snippet_en: GHG Emission Reduction Roadmap: operate bimonthly Net Zero Committee and Carbon Reduction Committee to establish and execute DS Division GHG reduction action items; expand process gas treatment facility (RCS) installation; reduce LNG boiler usage through expansion of waste heat recovery; develop/apply high efficiency RCS catalyst; expand the utilization of waste heat recovery system; develop innovative technologies for improving process gas treatment efficiency; improve energy efficiency of FAB facilities through cooperation with facility companies; achieve net zero Scope 1, 2 emissions for DS Division.

project_evidence.subtype_en: Demand acceleration for zero and low-carbon materials
project_evidence.project_name_en: WBCSD Center for Decarbonization Demand Acceleration founding-member initiative
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Collaborating through a strategic two-year initiative to turn market demand indicators into actions accelerating commercial adoption of zero and low-carbon materials
project_evidence.implementation_stage: founding-member initiative launched in 2024 with two-year horizon
project_evidence.cost_or_investment_review_note_en: Report does not disclose quantified cost or investment for this initiative in the snippet.
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report states the initiative is intended to accelerate commercial adoption of zero and low-carbon materials and align standards and certification schemes; quantified CO2e abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: LyondellBasell reports that in 2024 it became a founding member of WBCSD's Center for Decarbonization Demand Acceleration, launched during New York Climate Week. The report describes the CDDA as a strategic two-year initiative dedicated to turning market demand indicators into tangible actions that accelerate the commercial adoption of zero and low-carbon materials across industries, in collaboration with industry peers, value-chain partners, and organizations such as the Center for Green Market Activation and the Sustainable Procurement Pledge.

project_evidence.project_name_en: CarbonCure low-carbon concrete technology
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Deploying CarbonCure technology to inject CO2 into concrete, creating low-carbon concrete and permanent CO2 storage
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report states the technology creates low-carbon concrete and achieves permanent CO2 storage; quantified abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: Schneider Electric reports that CarbonCure's technology, deployed globally, injects CO2 into concrete to create low-carbon concrete, achieving permanent CO2 storage and demonstrating scalability as a climate solution. The same page also references the Mekong River Delta Water Purifier project and future AVEVA portfolio projects.

project_evidence.project_name_en: ACS low-carbon procurement lever
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Strengthening sustainable procurement with subcontractors, recycled and low-carbon materials, materials of biological origin, and low-carbon embedded equipment and vehicles
project_evidence.implementation_stage: decarbonization lever disclosed for Scope 3 reduction planning
project_evidence.cost_or_investment_review_note_en: Report does not disclose quantified procurement cost in this snippet.
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report maps low-carbon procurement measures to GHG Protocol Scope 3 subcategories 3.1 and 3.2; quantified CO2e abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: ACS lists low-carbon procurement as a decarbonization lever. Measures include strengthening sustainable procurement practices with subcontractors, recycled and low-carbon materials, materials of biological origin, and low-carbon embedded equipment and vehicles. The table maps these measures to Scope 3 subcategories according to the GHG Protocol, including 3.1 and 3.2.

project_evidence.project_name_en: Intel Green Bond project allocation
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Allocating green bond proceeds to HVAC upgrades, heat recovery, greenhouse gas abatement systems and water reclaim facility upgrades
project_evidence.implementation_stage: projects funded and reported in 2024 Green Bond Report
project_evidence.cost_or_investment_en: Cumulative USD 639 million allocation, about 51% of a USD 1.25 billion green bond issued in 2022.
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Project areas include energy efficiency, renewable electricity and greenhouse gas abatement systems; quantified CO2e abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: Intel states that in its second Annual Green Bond Report, published in 2024, it outlined the allocation of a cumulative USD 639 million, approximately 51% of a USD 1.25 billion green bond issued in 2022. Eligible project areas include pollution prevention and control, water stewardship, energy efficiency, renewable electricity, circular economy and waste management, and green buildings. Recent projects included HVAC upgrades and heat recovery projects, purchases of greenhouse gas abatement systems, and upgrades of water reclaim facilities in Arizona and Oregon.

The same passage also notes reducing energy consumption, increasing electrification in processes and buildings, and transforming the entire car fleet to 100% electric vehicles.

project_evidence.measure_name_en: Commissioned solar power plants with co-located battery storage in southeast Texas
project_evidence.snippet_en: In 2024, TotalEnergies commissioned Danish Fields (720 MW) and Cottonwood (455 MW), two solar power plants with co-located battery storage in southeast Texas. These new projects are part of a portfolio of more than 8 GW of renewable assets in operation in the country.

project_evidence.project_name_en: Korea DS Division solar PPA
project_evidence.measure_name_en: PPA with SK E&S and Samsung C&T for renewable energy from a 60 MW solar power plant
project_evidence.snippet_en: The DS Division signed a PPA with SK E&S in Nov. 2023 and with Samsung C&T in Mar. 2024 to supply approximately 76.2 GWh of renewable energy annually from a 60 MW solar power plant for 20 years for a total of 1,466 GWh of renewable energy, starting in 2025. So far, Samsung has installed a total of 2.8 MW of solar power generation facilities and generated 2.8 GWh of energy in 2023 for on-site use.

project_evidence.snippet_en: Cigna reports that it is sourcing renewables and purchasing Energy Attribute Certificates (EACs), committed to sourcing 100% renewable electricity by 2030, joined the global RE100 pledge in 2022, and by the end of 2024 sourced approximately 52% of its global power needs from renewable electricity. The report also states it continues to explore long-term renewable energy procurement agreements, including power purchase agreements and onsite renewables where plausible.

The report states that carbon intensity reduction in its proprietary real-estate equity and debt portfolio resulted from increased renewable energy utilization and energy-efficiency improvements. project_evidence.project_name_en: Design and materials roadmap
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Using recycled lithium, zinc, rare earth elements, and low-carbon materials in products
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report attributes 6.2M avoided emissions to low-carbon materials in the Apple comprehensive carbon footprint graphic.
project_evidence.snippet_en: We design our products to be less carbon intensive by prioritizing the use of recycled and renewable content and low-carbon materials. Our progress: More than doubled the use of certified recycled lithium and zinc shipped in our products in 2024. iPhone 16 uses more than 95 percent recycled lithium in the battery, a first for Apple.

project_evidence.subtype_en: Process gas treatment and process upgrade
project_evidence.project_name_en: DS Division process gas treatment expansion
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Expanded RCS process gas treatment facilities and high-efficiency RCS catalyst development
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report places process gas treatment expansion in the DS Division GHG Emission Reduction Roadmap and states the roadmap aims to achieve net zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions for the DS Division.
project_evidence.snippet_en: GHG Emission Reduction Roadmap: operate bimonthly Net Zero Committee and Carbon Reduction Committee to establish and execute DS Division GHG reduction action items; expand process gas treatment facility (RCS) installation; reduce LNG boiler usage through expansion of waste heat recovery; develop/apply high efficiency RCS catalyst; expand the utilization of waste heat recovery system; develop innovative technologies for improving process gas treatment efficiency; improve energy efficiency of FAB facilities through cooperation with facility companies; achieve net zero Scope 1, 2 emissions for DS Division.

project_evidence.company_name_zh: 利安德巴塞尔工业公司
project_evidence.subtype_en: Demand acceleration for zero and low-carbon materials
project_evidence.project_name_en: WBCSD Center for Decarbonization Demand Acceleration founding-member initiative
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Collaborating through a strategic two-year initiative to turn market demand indicators into actions accelerating commercial adoption of zero and low-carbon materials
project_evidence.implementation_stage: founding-member initiative launched in 2024 with two-year horizon
project_evidence.cost_or_investment_review_note_en: Report does not disclose quantified cost or investment for this initiative in the snippet.
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report states the initiative is intended to accelerate commercial adoption of zero and low-carbon materials and align standards and certification schemes; quantified CO2e abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: LyondellBasell reports that in 2024 it became a founding member of WBCSD's Center for Decarbonization Demand Acceleration, launched during New York Climate Week. The report describes the CDDA as a strategic two-year initiative dedicated to turning market demand indicators into tangible actions that accelerate the commercial adoption of zero and low-carbon materials across industries, in collaboration with industry peers, value-chain partners, and organizations such as the Center for Green Market Activation and the Sustainable Procurement Pledge.

project_evidence.project_name_en: CarbonCure low-carbon concrete technology
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Deploying CarbonCure technology to inject CO2 into concrete, creating low-carbon concrete and permanent CO2 storage
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report states the technology creates low-carbon concrete and achieves permanent CO2 storage; quantified abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: Schneider Electric reports that CarbonCure's technology, deployed globally, injects CO2 into concrete to create low-carbon concrete, achieving permanent CO2 storage and demonstrating scalability as a climate solution. The same page also references the Mekong River Delta Water Purifier project and future AVEVA portfolio projects.

project_evidence.project_name_en: ACS low-carbon procurement lever
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Strengthening sustainable procurement with subcontractors, recycled and low-carbon materials, materials of biological origin, and low-carbon embedded equipment and vehicles
project_evidence.implementation_stage: decarbonization lever disclosed for Scope 3 reduction planning
project_evidence.cost_or_investment_review_note_en: Report does not disclose quantified procurement cost in this snippet.
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report maps low-carbon procurement measures to GHG Protocol Scope 3 subcategories 3.1 and 3.2; quantified CO2e abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: ACS lists low-carbon procurement as a decarbonization lever. Measures include strengthening sustainable procurement practices with subcontractors, recycled and low-carbon materials, materials of biological origin, and low-carbon embedded equipment and vehicles. The table maps these measures to Scope 3 subcategories according to the GHG Protocol, including 3.1 and 3.2.

project_evidence.implementation_stage: projects funded and reported in 2024 Green Bond Report

Recent projects included HVAC upgrades and heat recovery projects, purchases of greenhouse gas abatement systems, and upgrades of water reclaim facilities in Arizona and Oregon.

project_evidence.project_name_en: Cleaner Fuel SAF scale-up
project_evidence.measure_name_en: SAF deliveries, long-term offtake agreements, Minnesota SAF Hub collaboration, and MSP blending facility launch
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report states 13M+ gallons of SAF uplifted in 2024 and 119,781 metric tons CO2e avoided.
project_evidence.snippet_en: Cleaner Fuel: Delta signed millions of gallons in long-term offtake agreements with existing and emerging SAF producers. In 2024, Delta more than tripled SAF deliveries compared to 2023, for a total of over 13 million gallons. Delta also collaborated through the Minnesota SAF Hub to produce the first-ever batch of Minnesota crop-based SAF and announced the launching of a SAF blending facility to serve MSP airport. The page states 13M+ gallons of SAF uplifted in 2024 and 119,781 metric tons CO2e avoided.

project_evidence.project_name_en: Renewable electricity for all Siemens Energy facilities
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Using renewable electricity in all facilities around the globe as a lever for climate-neutral operations
project_evidence.implementation_stage: target reached in fiscal year 2023 and maintained in operations
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report identifies renewable electricity in all facilities as one lever for reducing Siemens Energy's carbon footprint; quantified abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: Siemens Energy states that its goal is to be climate neutral within operations by 2030. One lever is using renewable electricity in all facilities around the globe, a target the company says it reached in fiscal year 2023. The same passage also notes reducing energy consumption, increasing electrification in processes and buildings, and transforming the entire car fleet to 100% electric vehicles.

project_evidence.project_name_en: La Cira Infantas solar farm
project_evidence.measure_name_en: 56 MWp solar farm in Barrancabermeja for self-consumption
project_evidence.cost_or_investment_en: Report states the initiative is part of a reduction of approximately USD 1.6 million in gas consumption.
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Expected to generate up to 76.3 GWh per year and reduce 18,000 tons of CO2 equivalent emissions at Barrancabermeja.
project_evidence.snippet_en: Ecopetrol states that in 2024 it inaugurated the La Cira Infantas solar farm in Barrancabermeja, with an installed capacity of 56 MWp for self-consumption, expected to generate up to 76.3 gigawatt-hours per year. The initiative is part of a reduction of approximately USD 1.6 million in gas consumption and 18,000 tons in CO2 equivalent emissions at Barrancabermeja.

project_evidence.subtype_en: Biomass and concentrated solar thermal at breweries
project_evidence.project_name_en: Brazil and Vietnam biomass use and Spain concentrated solar thermal breweries
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Using biomass at two large operating companies and concentrated solar thermal at two Spanish breweries
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report presents these as success cases for decarbonising operations; quantified abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: HEINEKEN reports success cases for decarbonising operations: two of its largest operating companies, Brazil and Vietnam, are using biomass, and two of its breweries in Spain are using concentrated solar thermal to harness the power of the sun.

project_evidence.project_name_en: 3M site conversion to 100% renewable electricity
project_evidence.measure_name_en: Converting sites worldwide to be powered by 100% renewable electricity and seeking solar, wind, and other alternative energy projects
project_evidence.implementation_stage: conversion program started in 2019 and reported through end-2024
project_evidence.cost_or_investment_review_note_en: Report does not disclose quantified site conversion cost in this snippet.
project_evidence.abatement_effect_en: Report states sites powered by 100% renewable electricity comprised 62.9% of total electricity use at the end of 2024; quantified CO2e abatement is not disclosed in this snippet.
project_evidence.snippet_en: 3M reports that its energy-footprint management includes evaluating and improving products, manufacturing processes, equipment, and sites. The report states that in 2019 3M began converting sites around the world to be powered by 100% renewable electricity. As of the end of 2024, sites powered by 100% renewable electricity comprised 62.9% of total electricity use, and 3M continues to seek alternative energy sources at sites, including solar, wind, and projects.

primary_secondary_data.display_policy_en: The main bubble chart draws only strong bubbles based on explicitly reported primary-data percentages. Method-row source-mix ratios are retained as inference review data and are not drawn as strong evidence.
primary_secondary_data.display_policy_zh: 主气泡图只绘制原文明示 primary data 百分比的强证据气泡；method_rows 来源结构比例保留为推断复核数据，不作为强证据绘制。
primary_secondary_data.policy_en: Bubble positions prefer explicit reported primary-data percentages when disclosed; otherwise method-row source mix remains inference review data rather than an audited calculation weight.
primary_secondary_data.policy_zh: 气泡位置优先使用原文明示的初级数据百分比；没有明示百分比时退回方法行来源结构比例。两者仍需计算权重核验。
